title: introduce-economy-sandbox-cli-and-rule-prober
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Add Economy Sandbox CLI: a local cost/econ simulator and rule prober for batching, cache, and quantization defaults. Includes synthetic workload generator, policy YAML integration, and web UI sample output. Intended for platform and SRE teams to validate unit-econ regressions before rollout.
body:
Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a lightweight way to simulate the downstream unit economics of configuration changes (batching, cache lifetimes, quant profiles) without spin-up of dedicated infra or long A/B tests. This PR introduces 'economy-sandbox', a CLI and small library used to run fast hypothesis tests against representative workload traces, to generate a cost-delta waterfall, latency safety envelope, and rule-prober output that can be consumed by Redwood Optimize and rollout tooling.

Summary of changes: 1) tools/economy-sandbox/ CLI (Go) with subcommands: 'simulate', 'probe-rules', 'profile-compare', and 'serve-ui'. 'simulate' accepts a short YAML describing a workload, model variants, and policy knobs; it runs a batched simulator that accounts for batching curves, cache hit-rate models, KV-cache warming costs, and quantized execution multipliers. 'probe-rules' takes policy-as-code and produces pass/fail and safety-score per rule. 'profile-compare' compares quant profiles (fp16,int8,4-bit-llm) and outputs a fidelity vs cost plot. 'serve-ui' spins up a tiny local web page to inspect the waterfall and trace-level breakdown. 2) library components in libs/econ-sim/: cost-model, batching-curves, cache-model, quant-penalties, synthetic-trace-generator. 3) Example configs and a small corpus of synthetic traces under tools/economy-sandbox/examples/ representing chat, summarization, and search-like workloads. 4) Documentation and quickstart in docs/economy-sandbox.md and a sample Linear task template for SEs. 5) Unit tests and end-to-end smoke tests for the CLI and web UI.

Key design notes: - The simulator is not a runtime emulator; it models latency distributions parametrically based on device profiles (g.gpu-v100, a100x, tpu) and empirically derived batching curves. - Cache model supports TTL and prefix/KV modes; prefill/warm policies are modeled as costs amortized across simulated requests. - Quant penalties model both throughput multipliers and quality deltas; we expose a user-provided fidelity function to estimate downstream eval loss (optional). - Policy rules are plain YAML with predicates (SLO, cost delta, quality delta, latency P95); probe produces a structured table and a human-readable remediation suggestion per failure.

Example usage: economy-sandbox simulate --config examples/chat-small.yaml --model-profile open-7b --quant-profile int8-fast --out report.json
The resulting report.json contains a cost_delta (%), expected tokens/sec, expected P50/P95 latency, and a rule_probes list with pass/fail and severity.

Commits (high-level): - add CLI skeleton and command parsing - implement cost-model and batching curves - add quant profile adapters and fidelity hook - implement synthetic trace generator and examples - add policy prober and YAML schema - add serve-ui and static assets - add docs and quickstart - tests and CI wiring

Files changed (high level): - tools/economy-sandbox/cmd/*.go - libs/econ-sim/*.go - tools/economy-sandbox/examples/*.yaml - docs/economy-sandbox.md - infra/ci/econ-sandbox-smoke.yml - web/econ-sandbox-ui/* - tests/econ-sim/*_test.go

Tests and CI: - Unit tests for cost-model, batching curves, cache-model and quant penalty math. - Integration smoke that runs 'simulate' against 3 example configs and validates outputs within expected tolerances. - UI snapshot test to ensure report rendering unchanged. CI checks initially failed on lint and a race in the synthetic trace generator; fixed by tightening goroutine shutdown and adding a deterministic seed. All checks now pass on main CI runner.

Review thread (highlights):
- Ava Martinez (reviewer): "Nice incremental design. Can we make the fidelity function pluggable as a Python bridge? Some teams have eval harnesses in Python."
  - Author reply: "We provide a simple gRPC hook (libs/econ-sim/fidelity_adapter) that accepts JSON and can be implemented by either Go or a lightweight Python service. Added example in examples/python-fidelity/."
- Ravi Singh: "Cache prefill cost amortization model looks optimistic for high-churn workloads."
  - Author reply: "Good call. Added 'churn_factor' to TTL model and a toggle to run pessimistic vs optimistic amortization in simulate. Updated examples to show both."
- Lena Cho: "Please ensure the CLI exits non-zero on rule probe failures when used in automation."
  - Author reply: "Added --fail-on-policy flag and a clear exit code mapping in the docs. CI now exercises this path."

Approvals: - Ava Martinez approved on 2026-01-26 - Ravi Singh approved on 2026-01-27

Risk and rollout: Low risk. This is tooling-only and does not change serving runtime behavior. The CLI is gated behind the tools path and is not included in production images by default. We added a short deprecation note and a feature flag to gate any future infra integration.

Follow-ups (tracked): - ENG-4824: Add historical trace import from production sampling to better fit batching curves - ENG-4825: Hook economy-sandbox reports into Redwood Optimize recommendations engine - PM-1150: UX polish for the serve-ui visualization and CSV export

Notes for cherry-picks: The changes in libs/econ-sim are additive; cherry-pick to release/* should be safe but the CI smoke job should be included to preserve deterministic seeds.

Merged using squash. Change log entry added to docs/release-notes/2026-01.md.

If you want to run locally: follow docs/economy-sandbox.md (quickstart) and run 'make econ-sandbox-smoke' which runs the smoke examples and produces reports in /tmp/econ-reports.
